faqs.a: Mechanically, pick either. Same platform, same drivetrains, same van underneath. The Vellfire looks meaner and the Alphard holds money slightly better here. Just check the one you're actually bidding on, because the register treats them as different cars.

Yes. The engines and hybrid gear are shared with Toyotas sold new in Australia, so any decent workshop can handle it. Body panels and interior trim are the slow parts, so factor that in on anything with damage on the sheet.

Australia sold the Hiace, so why import one? Three reasons, and they're the same three every time.

Japan got the 4WD diesel we never did. Japan got factory campervan conversions that would cost you a fortune to build here. And a Japanese van at 90,000km has been inspected every two years, while the Australian equivalent has spent a decade on building sites.

faqs.a: The twin turbo is the one everyone wants and it's priced accordingly. The naturally aspirated 2JZ-GE is a lot of money less and still a good car if you want the shape rather than the timeslip. Just make sure you know which one you're buying, because plenty have been converted.

Whether it's standard, and whether the odometer and the auction sheet agree. These have been modified and traded hard for thirty years. An untouched one is worth far more than a fast one and much harder to find.
Both generations were, which is why the register windows are specific rather than open. Upside is that local knowledge and some parts already exist.
